blk_part_01_part_1_curry_is_not_one_food.text: The word "curry" became popular through British colonial history. Indian food had many different regional dishes and spice mixtures, but the British simplified many of them under the word "curry." Later, curry powder became an easy spice mix that could travel around the world. Japanese curry came through this British version, not directly from ordinary Indian home cooking. House Foods explains that Japanese curry developed from Indian masala, moved through British curry powder, and then reached Japan.
